item.title: Ignited: Striking Industrial Automation Conversations: Why the Knowledge Model Is the Missing Layer in Your Industrial Data Architecture
item.description:
Most manufacturers have more data than they know what to do with, yet none of it speaks the same language or reflects how the factory actually operates. When operational issues arise, teams are often left calling specific individuals who hold critical system relationships entirely in their heads. In this episode, Travis and Tom sit down with Jeff Knepper and Graeme Welton from Flow Software, alongside Ryan Crownover from Vertech, to explore what it takes to build an industrial data architecture that goes beyond basic connectivity and dashboards. They discuss how a true knowledge model maps real-world relationships between assets, processes, people, systems, and events, fundamentally transforming raw operational data into actionable enterprise intelligence.

 

Guests:

  • Jeff Knepper (Flow Software)

  • Graeme Welton (Flow Software)

item.title: Planet Money: We try to fix election polling (update)
item.description:
Polling is facing an existential crisis. People aren't picking up the phone. Nobody wants to talk to pollsters. Trust is on the line. We pluck a solution from the economics canon and convince a polling firm to let us test it. 

Today on the show, we head to Marist College — home of the Marist Poll — to learn how to be pollsters ourselves. We learn the great moments in polling history, the latest science of polling, and find out all the tricks that pollsters use to get people to finish their surveys. Then we get on the phone and give it a try ourselves. And offer some of our own solutions. 

This episode was originally published before the 2022 midterm elections. 

We have an update on our idea to save polling, which Marist is still testing, and we find out what it might be able to tell us about the 2026 midterms.

item.title: Manufacturing Happy Hour: 307: Building the Factory of the Future - LIVE from Revere Electric's Executive Forum at UWM's Connected Systems Institute (Milwaukee, WI)
item.description:
Manufacturing has been collecting skills for centuries, and the list keeps growing.

Chris takes Manufacturing Happy Hour to Revere Electric’s Executive Forum at the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee (UWM) for a live conversation about what the factory of the future needs in the plant and in the workforce. Joining him are Michael Cvelbar and Phil Bush of Rockwell Automation, Joe Hamann of the Connected Systems Institute (CSI), and Ryan Schneeberger of Revere Electric Supply.

Joe and Phil look at how new people get job-ready through student hackathons and a veteran training program. Ryan and Michael cover the other side, keeping people on the floor and giving operators more to do once they’re there. Students learn where AI adds value, while manufacturers want to see the return before they invest. And a room full of manufacturers toasts every time they say “digital twin.”

In this episode, find out:

  • Why Michael says manufacturers need backup plans when disruption hits
  • How Rockwell is preparing operators to troubleshoot their own equipment
  • Why manufacturers say new engineering graduates can take years to reach full productivity
  • How Rockwell’s Academy of Advanced Manufacturing trains military veterans as controls technicians
  • What flexible automation can do for a customer and why manufacturers stay cautious on AI until the ROI is clear
  • How Phil, Joe, Ryan and Michael describe their factory of the future when the audience asks

item.title: Filmspotting: "I wonder what percent of people ever actually encounter a work of art that changes them" with Manohla Dargis | The Movie Racket
item.description:
Can a movie change your life? In a 1960s interview, Stanley Kubrick posed a deceptively simple provocation: "I wonder what percent of people ever actually encounter a work of art that changes them."

This week, New York Times Chief Film Critic Manohla Dargis joins Michael Phillips to test this proposition against a lifetime of moviegoing. Together, they reflect on films that expanded their sense of what cinema could do — from Jean-Luc Godard's Breathless and Every Man for Himself to Kubrick's own 2001: A Space Odyssey — and discuss the difference between a movie that alters your life and one that offers you a profound experience.

item.title: NerdWallet's Smart Money Podcast: Afraid to Ask for a Raise? Negotiate Your Salary With 5 Simple Words
item.description:
Learn how to get past the fear of negotiating for higher pay, even when your employer might say no.
Why does negotiating feel so scary, and how do you get past that fear? Hosts Sean Pyles, CFP®, and Elizabeth Ayoola talk with Kwame Christian, a negotiation expert, CEO of the American Negotiation Institute and host of the “Big Swings Only” podcast. They discuss how the fear of rejection, awkwardness and damaged relationships can keep you from asking for what you want, the everyday situations where you could negotiate more than you expect, and Kwame’s three-step framework for tough conversations. You’ll also hear what an “internal negotiation” with yourself looks like, how shifting from a fear of failure to a fear of regret could change your approach, and why staying quiet can turn into resentment.
And what do you do when the job offer seems final or your company says it doesn’t negotiate pay? Kwame walks Sean and Elizabeth through why it can help to think about total compensation instead of salary alone, the five-word question that could reveal room to move in an offer, how outside offers may give you leverage with your current employer, and how to respond to a “no negotiation” policy without attacking it. They also get into anchoring, why repeating the other side’s number can work against you, when raising your voice could backfire, and how to turn everyday negotiations into deliberate practice.

item.title: Where Should We Begin? with Esther Perel: Can I Still Be a Good Man if I Leave?
item.description:
After decades together, he wonders whether he can stay in a marriage where intimacy and connection has all but disappeared. He's touch-starved and lonely and questioning whether preserving the family unit for the sake of his young daughter, is worth the cost of losing himself. Esther helps him look beyond the question of whether to stay or leave and toward what he needs to feel alive and true to himself.
Esther Callings are a one time, 45-60 minute interventional phone call with Esther. They are edited for time, clarity, and anonymity. If you have a question you would like to talk through with Esther, send a voice memo to producer@estherperel.com.
Producer’s Note: When our anonymous guests do a session with Esther for the podcast, it is an act of generosity for everyone who listens. These sessions are meant not only to support the people in the room with Esther, but all of us who learn from their stories. Our stories have many chapters, and what you hear is just one moment in someone’s journey. So even though the sessions are anonymous, please remember that real people are behind them and they may be reading your comments.
Relationships are undergoing a massive cultural shift. We've never been more connected, and we've never felt more disconnected. We crave understanding and collective experience. We want to be seen but we're optimizing for isolation. Esther believes that the only way to improve our relationships is to remember the basics of being together. item.title: Planet Money: Anatomy of a movie market
item.description:

And even for those movies that make it into elite film festivals like Sundance – it can take everything from performance stunts to corporate spycraft to seal the deal. Today on the show, we follow the ‘King of Sundance’ as he and his team try to sell their slate of movies to distributors like Netflix and Sony and Apple. item.title: The Automation Ladies: Building Ignition: Colby Clegg on Innovation, AI, and the Future of Industrial Automation
item.description:
🫆 Thank you to our amazing sponsor Inductive Automation 

______________________________________________________________

Industrial automation doesn’t need more hype. It needs tools that solve real plant problems, survive real uptime demands, and still play nicely with modern IT. We sit down with Colby Clegg, CEO of Inductive Automation, to unpack how Ignition grew out of a systems integrator’s breaking point: the cost and pain of getting PLC data into SQL databases and into the hands of people who could actually use it.

From there, we zoom out on OT IT convergence and why the divide persists. We talk about OPC UA, open platforms, and the very different risk tolerances that shape engineering decisions on the plant floor versus the enterprise. Colby shares how Inductive hires a lot of software and computer science talent, then teaches the industrial context, and why that approach can challenge the “this is how we’ve always done it” mindset without ignoring the reality of downtime, compliance, and safety.

Finally, we get specific about what’s new: the arc from Ignition 8.3 toward Ignition 2027, the push for infrastructure independence with containerization, orchestration, and source control friendly configuration, and how that openness intersects with AI in manufacturing. We’re candid about the distance between impressive generative AI output and a production ready control system, why guardrails matter, and why legacy upgrades are becoming a cybersecurity issue, not just a maintenance task. If you enjoy the conversation, subscribe, share it with a friend in OT or IT, and leave a review so more automation folks can find the show.

item.title: NerdWallet's Smart Money Podcast: How to Plan a Sabbatical (and Pay for It), Plus the Hidden Costs of Cash Advance Apps
item.description:
Learn how to plan and pay for a sabbatical, plus why cash advance apps may cost more than you think.
How do you plan and pay for a sabbatical, even if your employer doesn't offer a paid one? Hosts Sean Pyles, CFP®, and Elizabeth Ayoola are joined by Smart Money producer Tess Vigeland to answer a listener's question about setting up for extended time off work. They talk about how rare paid sabbaticals are, which companies offer them, and how to set goals for your time away. Tess shares the story of her three-year sabbatical in Asia, and the hosts compare the pros and cons of shorter breaks. They also get into building a sabbatical budget and sinking fund, why debt and emergency savings matter even more when your paycheck pauses, what happens to your health insurance, and what it can feel like to return to work. Plus, ways to get a real break when a sabbatical isn't in reach.
Why might cash advance apps cost more than their marketing would lead you to believe? Senior news writer Anna Helhoski talks with Candice Wang, senior researcher at the Center for Responsible Lending, about new research on payday advance apps. They discuss how these apps differ from traditional payday lenders (and how they don’t), why users may not recognize them as high-cost loans, how an average 232% APR and frequent repeat borrowing can add up, why some state payday lending laws don't apply, and what you could consider before using one.
